events.factual_description: Billboard Live YOKOHAMA presents H ZETTRIO's “Speed Music Night with H ZETTRIO 2026” on Saturday, September 5, 2026. The first stage opens at 14:30 and starts at 15:30; the second opens at 17:30 and starts at 18:30. Billboard and H ZETTRIO's official page list the trio as H ZETT M on piano, H ZETT NIRE on bass and H ZETT KOU on drums. The official pages frame the show as the live extension of the TV Kanagawa project SPEED MUSIC ソクドノオンガク and show the 2026 series recurring quarterly at Billboard Live YOKOHAMA on February 27, June 7, September 5 and December 5. Billboard lists current seat charges ranging from ¥7,500 for Casual Side seats to ¥19,300 for a two-person DX Sheet DUO, with other seat categories between those amounts.

en.why_it_matters: The repertoire concept is the hook: H ZETTRIO takes Japanese songs from different eras and rebuilds them for piano, bass and drums, turning a long-running television project into a compact live songbook of speed, arrangement and trio interplay. That gives the Yokohama date a distinctly Japanese listening-history thread and a strong instrumental identity rather than making it just another piano-trio club set.
en.trip_verdict: If September 5 is open and Yokohama fits naturally into the Kanto plan, either set is worth catching. The two showtimes make it easy to fold into the day; I would keep scarcer farewells, premieres or rare master appearances ahead of it rather than reorganize the itinerary around this recurring showcase.

es.why_it_matters: El gancho está en el repertorio: H ZETTRIO toma canciones japonesas de distintas épocas y las reconstruye para piano, bajo y batería, convirtiendo un proyecto televisivo de larga duración en un cancionero en vivo de velocidad, arreglo e interacción de trío. Eso le da a la fecha de Yokohama un hilo muy japonés de historia de escucha y una identidad instrumental clara, en vez de ser simplemente otro set de piano trio.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 5 de septiembre está libre y Yokohama entra naturalmente en el plan de Kantō, cualquiera de los dos sets vale la pena. Los dos horarios facilitan acomodarlo en el día; mantendría por delante despedidas, estrenos o apariciones más escasas de grandes maestros en vez de reorganizar el itinerario alrededor de esta serie recurrente.
